<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with clean framing and memorable lines, so the decision turns on who controlled the shared examples and whose spine survived. Side B (PRO) did two pieces of decisive work. First, it repossessed Side A's own illustrations: Moses's power ran through deliberately insulated public authorities, and the residents whose blocks were condemned were not the electorate that approved it, which directly punctured A's "thoroughly democratic system" claim; Flint was then turned from A's poisoned-water hypothetical into a case of an appointed manager overriding an elected council, with voice supplying the reason to look and accountability supplying the fix. A's reply ("voice without detection is screaming into a recorder") was sharp but did not dislodge B's causal chain, since it was resident pressure that brought the independent testing. Second, B built a priority argument A never squarely answered: competence is measured against a target it cannot select and exercised under a warrant it cannot issue. A's best response — that most conflicts are empirical, not moral, and that a vote does not make a bad forecast true — mitigates but partly concedes, and A also conceded there is no expert method for the mill-town tradeoff and that legitimacy is necessary. B's pressure question ("name the body that may overrule a legislature") extracted a real concession, and though A's turn of the accountant analogy (ownership without correctness) was the best moment of its case, "revocation is usually unwise" is advice, which B's closing named accurately. A did land hard on B's weakest seam — B conceded voters cannot detect error and that experts write the menu, so the firing mechanism looks epistemically hollow — and A used last word well ("hurts them lawfully," the owner burning his own building). But A left B's "without legitimacy you only have a memo" claim unattacked (no competent-but-unelected-regime counterexample), and A's second rebuttal was clipped over the word cap, costing it the weighing sentence at the crux. Narrow but real edge to B.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's recapture of Flint and Moses: showing that A's flagship "expert failure" was insulated authority imposed over an elected council, and that independent testing arrived because residents would not stop shouting, converted A's strongest concrete evidence into B's own illustration while A's "detection first, politics followed" reply left the trigger for detection unexplained.</best_rebuttal>
